title: IngestionCheckpoint
description: The resumable state of one dataset job: where the last run stopped and how it went. A DIRECT CONTRACT FOR data.job (provider, dataset, subject, mode, schedule_seconds, priority, enabled, cursor, last_success, last_attempt, status, retry_count) whose UNIQUE tuple (provider, dataset, subject, mode) is the job identity - EnsureJobs upserts schedule/priority/enabled and deliberately leaves cursor and last_* alone, because those are runtime state the engine owns. IMPORTANT GAP: plan §14 names last_block, last_timestamp and error_count as checkpoint fields, and data.job HAS NO SUCH COLUMNS - the block and timestamp cursors live inside the opaque `cursor` jsonb, and the error counter is retry_count. They are surfaced here as optional fields because a checkpoint contract must be readable without decoding a provider-specific jsonb blob; making them real columns is a schema decision, not an adapter decision.

subject.description: The per-subject partition of a dataset (a pool address, a feed slug). Defaults to the empty string in data.job, so an unpartitioned job and a job whose subject is '' are the same row.

mode.description: How the job fetches: 'poll' by default in data.job, plus the streaming modes the engine supports.

last_block.description: plan §14 block cursor. NO COLUMN EXISTS in data.job today - it is carried inside `cursor`. Present here so a checkpoint is readable without decoding the blob.

last_timestamp.description: plan §14 timestamp cursor. As with last_block, no dedicated column exists today.

last_success.description: Maps to data.job.last_success: when the last run SUCCEEDED. Distinct from last_attempt, and the difference is the whole staleness signal.

last_attempt.description: Maps to data.job.last_attempt: when the last run STARTED, successful or not.

status.description: data.job.status, defaulting to 'idle'. Health is read from HERE plus data.ingestion_run, never duplicated onto the source registry.

retry_count.description: Maps to data.job.retry_count - this is the plan's error_count; there is no separate error counter.

error_count.description: plan §14 spelling of the same counter. Non-null only when a producer wants the plan's name; it MUST equal retry_count when both are present, and the engine writes retry_count.

schedule_seconds.description: Declared by the job registry, not runtime state; EnsureJobs owns it and a run must not rewrite it.

priority.description: plan §28/§57: the scheduler's tiebreaker, so a premium-credit provider is not spent on a low-value pool.

enabled.description: False parks a job without deleting its cursor, so re-enabling resumes rather than re-backfills.
